newsitem.title: USA: Tiny blast near abortion clinic alarms Washington.
newsitem.headline: Tiny blast near abortion clinic alarms Washington.

text.p: A tiny explosion near an abortion clinic sent a wave of security jitters and protest cries through Washington Wednesday but police said it had the force of a firecracker and seemed unrelated to anti-abortion protests in the capital.

Although the only injury was a scratch on the hand of a passerby who found the mysterious device in a street a few blocks from the White House, the episode sparked security concerns - and furious protests from abortion rights groups -- because it occurred on the 24th anniversary of the Supreme Court decision legalising abortion.

Anti-abortion groups always mark the occasion with a mass Washington rally and march to the high court. There were also erroneous reports a second "explosive device" had been found near a hotel where Hillary Rodham Clinton and Vice President Al Gore were to attend an abortion-rights meeting.

President Bill Clinton, pressed for comment as he left on a trip to Chicago, issued a solemn denunciation of those who use terrorism to suppress legal rights -- although he also cautioned that "the facts are (still) unfolding."
Within a few hours police -- aided by FBI experts called in to help -- said it all appeared to be a false alarm.
They said they were were still trying to confirm their estimates of exactly what the device was and to discover who left it at the base of a downtown street lamp.

"It appears as though it might have been there for awhile," Police Chief Larry Soulsby said at a news conference. "We have nothing to indicate that its related to what is happening in town this week."

By that time, however, abortion-rights and feminist groups had issued a barrage of protests, alleging that the Washington incident was only the latest in efforts by anti-abortion forces to impose their views by violence and intimidation.
That drew protests from repesentatives of the "pro-life" anti-abortion groups gathered for the annual protest.

"Abortion advocates have jumped at the chance to blame pro-lifers for these incidents. The individuals responsible for these crimes are not pro-life and should be punished for their actions," said Carmen Pate of Concerned Women for America.
Soulsby said examinations of the debris at the scene "reveal that it could be an M-228 fuse assembly device used for (military) training purposes."
He said similar devices might be available in surplus stores and were not illegal.

James Biggar, general manager of the nearby Mayflower Hotel where Gore and Mrs. Clinton were to address an abortion rights group, said an unidentified overnight shift employee found the device while waiting for a bus to go home shortly before 8 a.m. (1300 GMT).
He said the man found the device at the base of a lamp post, picked it up and suffered scratches when it exploded.
The man returned to the hotel and told security guards what happened, dropping bits of the device along the way. This led to reports of a second suspicious device.

Bomb-sniffing dogs prowled through the hotel ballroom where Gore and Mrs. Clinton were to speak, rear and side doors were locked and metal detectors moved to the hotel as police stepped up security around the centre of Washington.
The incident was about 100 yards from the Planned Parenthood of Washington clinic where abortions are performed.
Rosanne Wisman, director of the Washington Planned Parenthood clinic across the street from where the device exploded, said, "It shook us up."
"For all the people involved in women's rights issues, it just makes us really angry that we have to worry about this."
As he left for Chicago, Clinton said, "Whatever happened, there is never an excuse for crimes of violence against someone exercising a consitutional right."
